name: uses parentheses for lower precedence but not left equal precedence
input: multiplication over addition and a left-nested subtraction
test:
assert serialize_expression(('*', ('+', 'a', 'b'), 'c')) == '(a+b)*c'
assert serialize_expression(('-', ('+', 'a', 'b'), 'c')) == 'a+b-c'
assert serialize_expression(('/', ('*', 'a', 'b'), 'c')) == 'a*b/c'
assert serialize_expression('value') == 'value'

name: preserves every right-nested equal-precedence tree
input: right children rooted at plus, minus, multiply, and divide
test:
assert serialize_expression(('+', 'a', ('+', 'b', 'c'))) == 'a+(b+c)'
assert serialize_expression(('+', 'a', ('-', 'b', 'c'))) == 'a+(b-c)'
assert serialize_expression(('*', 'a', ('*', 'b', 'c'))) == 'a*(b*c)'
assert serialize_expression(('/', 'a', ('*', 'b', 'c'))) == 'a/(b*c)'
assert serialize_expression(('/', 'a', ('/', 'b', 'c'))) == 'a/(b/c)'

name: round trips to the original tree without redundant grouping
